quote: My younger self did not realize that solving a mystery should make it feel less confusing.
content: The criterion is about confusion, not strangeness. Before quantum theory, black-body spectra were confusing in the essay's sense: the best models predicted infinite energy. Afterwards they are predicted to many decimal places, and what remains strange is how the world is, not what it will do. The part of quantum mechanics that still confuses experts, the measurement problem, is the part that is still unsolved. That is the essay's diagnostic working: leftover confusion marks leftover ignorance. "Nobody understands quantum mechanics" reports unfamiliarity. A solved mystery that leaves you able to predict everything it covers is less confusing, however weird it remains.

quote: Only then did I realize how reasonable vitalism had seemed at the time
content: The two essays describe the same error from outside and from inside. Kelvin's own words, "infinitely beyond the range of any scientific inquiry," justify the earlier description of cherished ignorance. This essay adds that the error felt reasonable to the people making it, which is why the young author made it too. The essay says so outright: "I thought the lesson of history was that astrologers and alchemists and vitalists had an innate character flaw." That belief is named and withdrawn as a lesson about character, while the description of what vitalism did stands. An error can seem reasonable and still be an embrace of mystery, and that is how it recruits intelligent people.

quote: right up until science finally solved them
content: The "life" that vitalism set out to explain, why living matter moves, grows, metabolizes and reproduces, has been explained; molecular biology answered it. The origin of life is a different question, and so are the others on the note's list. The induction is not that every mystery will be solved. It is that among the mysteries that were solved, the answer was never mysterious, and among those not yet solved, no mysterious answer has paid rent in the meantime. There is no survivorship error in a base rate whose failures are all open cases with no successful mysterious answer among them.
